review_candidates.description: Job Description Background: UN Women, grounded in the vision of equality enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations, works for the elimination of discrimination against women and girls; the empowerment of women; and the achievement of equality between women and men as partners and beneficiaries of development, human rights, humanitarian action and peace and security. Under its existing Strategic Note 2024-2028, PNG Country Office continues to deliver programmes that are aligned to global norms, policies and standards under four thematic areas; Women’s leadership and political participation; Women’s Economic Empowerment; Ending Violence Against Women; Women, Peace, Security and Humanitarian Actions UN Women’s work on economic empowerment has focused on strengthening informal economy markets- their management, working conditions, recovering women’s incomes and opportunities for business diversification. UN Women has continued to contribute to improving working conditions for women informal traders through capacity building for market managers, promoting women’s inclusion in governance, and raising public awareness of hygiene and women’s rights. Furthermore, UN Women has supported recovery of women’s incomes through financial literacy, business skills development and access to finance. Key to labour force participation and employment rates for women is their engagement in agriculture and fishing for household consumption in rural areas, where some 87 per cent of the population is concentrated. Limited access to formal sector opportunities restricts economic growth, especially for women, who face both formal and sociocultural barriers to formal employment, including GBV [i] . As a result, most women engage only in the informal sector, primarily in agriculture and micro- and small-scale retail. Meanwhile, women who enter the formal sector struggle to reach management level: just 13.8% of firms had a woman as a top manager in 2015. Estimates indicate that if women had equal employment opportunities, PNG’s GDP per capita could be 20.8% higher. Financial inclusion is growing rapidly across the country, partly because of the expansion of mobile banking services, but as with economic participation, women’s financial inclusion lags behind men’s. Although financial institutions, including microfinance institutions, are making inroads with new products and in reaching underserved populations, many small business owners (particularly women working informally) struggle to access formal credit. [i] Papua New Guinea Country Gender Assessment, UN Women ADB 2026 Engagement of the private sector is critical is accelerating gender equality, especially unlocking women’s potentials. It is evident that businesses influence women's access to formal employment, equal pay, safe workplaces, leadership positions, financial services and markets. UN Women's Women's Empowerment Principles (WEPs) — a joint initiative with the UN Global Compact — provide companies with practical guidance on how to empower women in the workplace, marketplace and community. To date, private sector engagement in PNG has been limited and ad hoc, and there is a need for a coherent, evidence-based strategy to build durable partnerships with businesses that can champion and resource gender equality outcomes. In addition, despite PNG's rich natural resource base and economic growth potential, gender inequality remains pervasive. Women face significant barriers to accessing financial services, economic opportunities and resources, with deep structural, cultural and legal constraints limiting their full participation in the economy. The financing landscape for gender equality and women’s empowerment in PNG remains fragmented, with limited domestic public financing, restricted access to private sector capital for women-led enterprises and constrained international development assistance UN Women is seeking to engage a consultant to lead the design of the women’s economic empowerment strategy in alignment with agreed priorities in the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (2024-2028). In particular, the role requires strong knowledge and experience in developing and implementing initiatives focused on business development and women’s financial inclusion, women’s voice and agency and social protection. It also requires supporting and developing mutually reinforcing partnerships with relevant regional bodies, Government counterparts, UN organisations, private sector, financial institutions, and CSOs – including deeper understanding of emerging issues in financing for gender equality. Develop a private sector engagement strategy and partnership framework, including a prioritized pipeline of potential partners and clear value propositions for engagement. Support the establishment of platforms such as the private sector roundtable, to facilitate dialogue and build relationships between UN Women, companies, business chambers and relevant government/employer bodies including Business Coalition for Women, PNG Chamber of Commerce and Industry, etc. Deliverable 3— Gender Financing Models Analysis, and Report, Policy Brief and Presentation Package. Develop a suite of gender financing models tailored to the PNG context, drawing on international best practice and the evidence Models should address a range of financing instruments and mechanisms including gender-responsive budgeting, blended finance, impact investing, women-focused microfinance, donor pooled funds and private sector partnerships. Each model should include a detailed implementation framework covering institutional arrangements, resource mobilisation strategies, monitoring and accountability mechanisms and sustainability pathways. Draft Gender Financing Models Report including full model descriptions, implementation frameworks and resource mobilisation recommendations. Experience supporting employee relocations, international assignments, work permits, visa administration, or expatriate management. Exposure to multinational organizations or multi-country operations is preferred. Experience working with external vendors such as immigration consultants, relocation providers, or tax advisors is an advantage. Skills & Knowledge Good understanding of global mobility policies, relocation practices, and assignment administration. Knowledge of immigration and work authorization processes across multiple countries is preferred. Familiarity with employment regulations, mobility compliance requirements, and HR operational processes. Understanding of mobility-related compensation, allowances, and employee benefits is advantageous. Behavioral Traits Analytical Skills Ability to analyze and interpret mobility-related data and identify potential issues or trends. Strong problem-solving skills with attention to detail. Communication & Interpersonal Skills Effective verbal and written communication skills. Ability to build positive working relationships with employees, managers, vendors, and stakeholders. Customer-service mindset with the ability to handle employee queries professionally. Planning & Organization Strong coordination and time management skills. Ability to manage multiple mobility cases concurrently while meeting deadlines. Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced environment. Compliance & Confidentiality High level of professionalism and integrity when handling confidential employee information. Strong awareness of compliance and governance requirements. Ability to identify and escalate potential risks appropriately. a Necessity, not a Luxury

review_candidates.title: Project Associate – Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS)
review_candidates.description: Job Description Introduction Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations and the leading UN agency in the field of migration. Working closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners, IOM promotes humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants. IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move. IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration Applications are welcome from internal and external candidates. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those of qualified and eligible second-tier candidates in the selection process. For the purpose of this vacancy, internal and internal-equivalent candidates are considered as first-tier candidates. Organizational Context and Scope The International Organization for Migration (IOM) Ireland has been operating in Ireland since 2001, currently in following areas of migration management: Assisted Voluntary Return and Reintegration (AVRR), Resettlement, Family Reunification, Counter-Trafficking (CT), Protection, Integration Support to Beneficiaries of Temporary Protection, Integrated Immigration Governance and Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS). IOM provides mental health and psychosocial support to international protection seekers residing in the Citywest accommodation facility with the aim to improve their psychosocial well-being and to strengthen their overall resilience. Under the overall supervision of the Chief of Mission (CoM) and the direct supervision of the National MHPSS Officer, the Project Associate – Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) will be responsible and accountable for providing efficient programmatic, financial assistance and support, including the day-to-day administrative, Human Resources (HR) and finance tasks related to the implementation of the MHPSS project. Responsibilities Assist the supervisor in implementing and monitoring the administrative, financial and HR activities related to the project, including supporting programme coordination tasks such as maintaining updated activity tracking tools and preparing short internal updates when requested, and providing day-to-day guidance to the two G-4 Programme Assistants to support consistent delivery of administrative and programme support functions. Implement delegated administrative actions in accordance with IOM rules, regulations and instructions to support compliant and timely processing of project-related administrative requirements. Maintain administrative, HR documents, as well as programme documentation including activity records, beneficiary statistics, financial tracking sheets in an organised and accessible manner to support retrieval of accurate information for project implementation, monitoring and reporting. Process staff expense claims and travel claims of the MHPSS Project staff per IOM rules and procedures to facilitate timely processing of staff-related administrative transactions. Assist in purchasing the items necessary for the project’s implementation in accordance with IOM rules and procedures for availability of goods and services required for project activities. Follow up and monitor internal administrative and financial processes with relevant units as well as project expenditures against approved budget lines by flagging discrepancies to the supervisor and site coordinators to support appropriate expenditure monitoring and timely resolution of administrative and financial issues. Assist the supervisor with coordinating administrative and HR functions related to the project, including compiling data and documentation required for donor reporting and reviewing information for completeness and accuracy to support timely submission of project-related reporting requirements. Coordinate office support services for meetings, trainings, seminars, committees, and special projects and events led by the supervisor. Attend meetings, prepare minutes, monitor follow-up activities and make arrangements for formal editing, translation, etc., of documents and publications. Perform such other relevant duties as maybe assigned. Qualifications Required Qualifications and Experience Education Bachelor’s degree in Political or Social Sciences, International Relations, Development Studies, Migration Studies, Human Rights, Law or a related field from an accredited academic institution with three years of relevant professional experience; or, High School diploma with five years of relevant experience. Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database. Experience Proven experience in a similar setting and capacity; Excellent knowledge of information technology and proficiency in Microsoft Office applications especially Excel, Word, PowerPoint; Experience with EU and/or international funding instruments, in financial management and reporting, accounting, budgeting and internal controls; Demonstrated ability to maintain accuracy & confidentiality in performing responsibilities; Strong interpersonal & intercultural skills with an attention to detail; and, Previous work experience in international organizations and service industry companies would be an advantage. Skills Interpersonal skills (i.e. empathy and emotional resilience); and, Knowledge of financial, administrative and human resources matters. Languages All IOM staff members in all categories are required to be fluent in one of the IOM's official languages (English, French, Spanish). For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written). Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments. Required Competencies IOM’s competency framework can be found at this link . Competencies will be assessed during the selection process. Values - all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values: Inclusion and respect for diversity: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion. Integrity and transparency: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct. Professionalism: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges. Courage: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance. Empathy: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated. Core Competencies – behavioural indicators Level 1 Teamwork: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results. Delivering results: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes. Managing and sharing knowledge: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate. Accountability: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work. Communication: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way. Notes Please refer to this link for guidance on IOM Job Category. Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation. This selection process may be used to staff similar positions in various duty stations. Recommended candidates will remain eligible to be appointed in a similar position for a period of 24 months. Appointment will be subject to certification that the candidate is medically fit for appointment, accreditation, any residency or visa requirements, security clearances. This post is subject to local recruitment. Only those holding a valid residence and work permit for the country where this position is based will be eligible for consideration. As the right to live and work in Ireland is required, the contract issued may be shorter that the period mentioned in the advertisement, in order to align with the expiry date of the work permit. IOM has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the United Nations and IOM, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment, abuse of authority and discrimination based on gender, nationality, age, race, sexual orientation, religious or ethnic background or disabilities. IOM does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process (application, interview, processing, training or other fee). IOM does not request any information related to bank accounts. IOM only accepts duly completed applications submitted through the IOM e-Recruitment system (for internal candidates link here ). The online tool also allows candidates to track the status of their application. No late applications will be accepted. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. For further information and other job postings, you are welcome to visit our website: IOM Careers and Job Vacancies
